Scene: At a branching deeper Backrooms corridor, THREE exhausted adult explorers have just realized they have walked in a circle. Center-right a young adult male in dusty work clothes has dropped his pack, collapsed to his knees and is clutching both sides of his head in unmistakable panic, mouth open. His female companion kneels, trying to bring his gaze back to hers, her own face frightened; their third companion at far right is pulling urgently at her shoulder and staring over his shoulder into a black side passage. Scene: An uncanny encounter with a harmless human echo: deep in an abandoned institutional break room, a familiar older adult colony worker in a faded red scarf sits calmly at a table set for four, as if lunch is about to begin. His plain work uniform, gentle ordinary face and completely relaxed posture are profoundly out of place. Two adult expedition members on the right recognize him as a colleague they left safely at their home colony. One has recoiled so hard a metal cup has fallen from her hand; her partner holds her back with a protective open arm, staring in frightened disbelief. Do not depict a copy of either explorer: the seated man is a distinct third person, not their own duplicate. The seated echo makes no threatening movement and holds no weapon. Three untouched plates and an empty chair pulled out toward the crew imply an invitation nobody wants to accept. Faded mint cafeteria walls, ochre floor, one flickering-looking still fluorescent light. Tight emotional tension, not a fight. No blood.

Scene: In a disturbing abandoned medical ward inside the Backrooms, an exhausted adult survivor sits rigidly at the far right edge of a cot, shoes still on, staring down with hands clasped and refusing eye contact.
